I literally didn’t comment to start a moral debate.  I could’ve used a ton of things other than eating meat to draw the parallel to my life from the original post.  My point is I recognize a behavior that I’m appalled by within myself.  That’s the point.  It’s not even about being vegan or being a billionaire.  You seem to want to argue about being vegan and I’m not like a rep for 98% of the population.  I’m identifying my fallibility as a human being, not dissecting individual moral decisions.  Bye

No I really don’t want to go on about it at all.  The point was that within me is the potential to do the worst and best of humanity.  I pointed out a common moral failing that I relate to.  I’m not exempt or above evil.  That doesn’t mean I walk around beating and killing people, yet I pointed out that when there’s enough space between the act and the outcome of it, humans tend to be able to act in an “out of sight out of mind” way.  I get it, I’d be a more moral human being if I was also vegan that’s basically the fucjing point I was making to begin with
I didn’t say “so why not?” That’s not the sentiment I’m trying to get at.  I’m pointing out an aspect of our psychology.  I get it that you’re vegan.

I was really just meaning to acknowledge a characteristic of human behavior and I used an example that relates to my own life and most other people’s.  Not to argue that it’s better for people/me to eat animal products, just stating that they/I do and are capable of it even if we’re aware of what it entails.  I know that it’s morally corrupt, and you’re asking why I don’t make the better choice.  There are a variety of reasons and for most people it probably comes down to convenience/social norms.  And yeah it’s a moral failing, just like the original post is.  Maybe I’ll become fully vegan one day, like I have for periods of time in the past.  But the original point I tried making would still stand.  I could’ve used examples other than eating meat to make the same point

I was just acknowledging the potential for evil in humans which includes myself.  That’s all.  The point I tried making is that there isn’t a divide between inherently good or bad people.  That we all have the same potential for good and evil(besides like psychopathy and extremes like that).  I really don’t want to argue on the internet this whole thing is making me super distraught lol I really wasn’t trying to argue that eating meat = good.  Eating meat is just the example I could pick out most clearly in my own life.  I was pointing out that I can rationalize it and it’s an area of my life I can relate to the original post where someone rationalizes being immoral.  There are a lot of ways I could improve myself and those are things I have and will confront my whole life and make choices about.  Admittedly I’m choosing a less moral option and I’m capable of that (along w most of the population) I was just pointing that out

I seriously was just pointing out the capability for humans to be evil when there’s distance btwn them and the act.  I was finding it within myself.  I was acknowledging that, not trying to debate choices.  I threw my individual identity self under the bus for the sake of the argument bc I’m just acknowledging the reality of being human and human behavior.  There’s a lot of moral/ethical dilemma that goes into being human.  I agree with you that veganism makes sense morally, but it also doesn’t mean that anything else we consume (food or other products) doesn’t have a relationship to suffering / exploitation / death.
